attribution_limitations: The route by which the infection reached the cervical spine is described as hematogenous in the Introduction and Discussion but as contiguous spread of existing OM in a later Discussion paragraph.
The same cervical CT (HD 27) is described as showing disc space destruction in the text and disc space narrowing in the Figure 2a caption.

Source conflict on certainty: the abstract says imaging confirmed compressive myelopathy, while the MRI text says the stenosis indicates possible compressive myelopathy and the HD 52 CT text says probable spinal cord compression; no body sentence confirms it.

The text gives AIS motor scores (46 at HD 42, 20 by HD 52, 54 over one year) without naming the Table 1 rows; Table 1 has Total Motor Score, Upper Extremity Motor Score and Lower Extremity Motor Score rows, and at HD52 both UEMS and TMS print 20.

High-flow oxygen therapy is dated HD 42 in the rehabilitation paragraph, while the earlier paragraph describes nasal oxygen first and then enhancement to high-flow after the MRI paragraph content, without a day.
"Presentation" in "four months prior to presentation" is not tied to a stated date or hospital day; the admission for prosthetic rehabilitation is the following sentence.
C-reactive protein is described as elevated (no day) and as increased by HD 44 in the text, while Table 1 gives 24.07 mg/L at HD 42 and 1.28 mg/L at 5 month follow-up.
The HD 52 CT text says "probable spinal cord compression", while the Figure 2c caption says "evidence of spinal cord compression" without the hedge.

Some CT findings stated only in the case text (foraminal stenosis at C6-7 and C5-6; kyphosis progression) belong to studies the text cites as Figure 2a/2c, but neither their sentences nor the captions give their hospital day.

claims.text: A 62-year-old male with diabetes mellitus, coronary artery occlusive disease, nonST elevation myocardial infarction, peripheral artery occlusive disease, chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, asthma and subclinical hypothyroidism had chronic osteomyelitis of the right foot and underwent right below-knee amputation four months before presentation. He was admitted to a rehabilitation department for comprehensive prosthetic rehabilitation therapy and complained of neck pain on hospital day 20.

MRI on HD 44 showed C6-7 changes consistent with osteomyelitis.
